images.title: Three different pieces
images.purpose: Set up the puzzle: fill one whole circle with exactly three fractional units, all different, starting from the biggest unit, 1/2.
images.composition: One large circle on the left with wide space around it, and a short column of text lines on the right.
images.exact_structure: Left: one large flat circle, the whole, with a dark outline. One teal #0072B2 sector fills exactly one half of the circle (180 degrees), on the left side. The other half is empty, outlined with a reddish purple #CC79A7 dashed line, with no lines drawn inside it. Right: three short text lines stacked with wide spacing. No other pieces drawn. Exactly 1 circle, 1 teal half, 1 empty half.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any line, piece or fraction drawn inside the empty half
images.takeaway: Three different units must fill exactly one whole.
images.description: A circle with a teal half placed and the other half empty and dashed; the student must fill the rest with two more fractional units, all three different. No answer is shown.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say why the empty half cannot be filled with two pieces of 1/4.

image_decisions.why: A circle with one half placed sets up the puzzle visually without showing the missing units.
